$comment: R1738 — WHICH SECTIONS OF THE ASSEMBLED APPLICATION ARE JUDGED, and for
each that is not, the reason that was accepted.
WHAT THIS PIN IS A CLAIM ABOUT, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The sibling pins
(`analyzer-rail-spec.json`, `analyzer-keys-spec.json`,
`analyzer-logs-spec.json`, `analyzer-inspector-spec.json`,
`analyzer-board-spec.json`) are claims about the BEHAVIOUR REFERENCE —
what it draws, in neutral vocabulary, written from an extraction. This one
is not. It is a claim about THIS BUILD: of the sections the reference
opens, which ones this application can currently say anything about.
It therefore does not repeat the seat list. The population is
`analyzer-rail-spec.json`'s canon, read from there, and this file holds
only the remainder — because a second copy of the eight seats is how two
screens of this tool came to disagree about what the tool contains, and
the fix for that was not another list.
WHAT FORCED IT. Measured over the wire at R1738, standing in each section
of the running application in turn: the application's own `conformance`
slot answered `specified 8, reproduced 8` from every one of them. That is
true about the RAIL. Read as a statement about the tool — which is how it
reads — it was wrong: two of the six open sections published a verdict
about their own surfaces, four published nothing, and no slot, test or
report anywhere named the other four. They were not failing a check; they
were absent from the population.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED. `scene`-side, `ScreenRoster::conformance` builds one
row per destination FROM THE ROSTER, so a section is missing from the
report only by not being in the application. Gate-side, the entries below
are asserted EQUAL to the application's unjudged rows — so a section that
starts answering must have its entry DELETED here, and an entry left
behind fails exactly as loudly as a section that went silent. A remainder
list that only ever grows is a remainder list nobody reads.
THE TWO KINDS BELOW ARE DIFFERENT WORK. `inline` is a page the host paints
itself, so the roster has no screen to ask; closing it means giving that
page a `Screen` of its own, which is what the trait being public is for.
`unspecified` is a mounted screen that publishes no verdict.
R1742 CLOSED `lab`, which was the second kind of `unspecified` — a screen
with a written specification it compared itself against inside a unit test
of its own binary, where the assembled application could not see it. Its
entry is DELETED rather than marked done, because the entries here are
asserted equal to the application's unjudged rows and a paid entry left
behind fails as loudly as a section that went silent. What made it the
hardest of the four is what the round had to decide: its surfaces exist
only once a session has selected a card and opened a roster, so its verdict
is about a session rather than about the build. A screen now says which of
its specified surfaces are NOT ON SCREEN and why, that count is part of the
verdict, and a report holding one does not reconcile — so the honesty is
structural rather than a promise. See `pinion_core::conformance::Built`.
★★★★★ R1747 CLOSED `packets`, AND CORRECTED WHAT THIS FILE SAID ABOUT IT.
The deleted entry read: *the capture viewer has no written specification at
all — not one unpublished, one unwritten*. That sentence was FALSE when
R1738 wrote it and stayed false for nine rounds. Re-measured 2026-08-20 by
listing the crate's modules and grepping the tree for the hook: R1663 wrote
screen B's specification as a value in that crate's `spec` module and its
`painted` module already ran the real view and layout passes and compared
the painted scene against it in both directions. Both predate the entry.
What was true is the OTHER half of the same sentence — those modules are
`#[cfg(test)]` and the binding implemented no `conformance` hook — so this
was *one unpublished*, the same shape `lab` was in, and the entry misnamed
which of the two kinds it was.
The lesson is the one this project keeps paying for and it is written here
rather than only in a round's ledger: A REASON RECORDED IN A REMAINDER IS
NOT RE-MEASURED BY THE THING THAT ENFORCES IT. The gate below asserts the
KEYS equal the application's unjudged rows and can say nothing at all about
the `why` beside them, so a wrong reason survives every push that a right
one would. Anything acting on one of these entries re-measures it first.
Both remaining entries are the `inline` kind, so the `unspecified` kind now
has no live case. The bottom remainder stays open anyway: the type is
unchanged, and the next screen with a specification it cannot publish yet
would be silent in exactly the same way.

owed.sentence: the host paints this page itself, so there is no screen to ask
why: The board is the shell's own view code rather than a mounted
screen, so the roster has nothing to ask. The route is not a new
mechanism: `pinion_screen::Screen` is public precisely for a host's
inline page, and giving the board one would make it answerable the
same way the four mounts are. It is a refactor of a 16.9k-line
binding and is its own round.

owed.sentence: the host paints this page itself, so there is no screen to ask
why: The same shape as `dashboard` and it would be closed by the same
edit. Listed separately rather than folded into one entry, because a
ledger whose entries do not correspond one-to-one with the rows they
excuse cannot be asserted equal to them.

owed.sentence: an unjudged section's row carries the host's reason, not the screen's
why: `SectionStanding::Unspecified` is what a host can see: this screen
published no verdict. Whether that is because nobody wrote a
specification or because one exists and is checked somewhere the
application cannot reach is a fact only the screen has, and the hook
it would answer through returns `Option<DocumentReport>` — which has
room for a report and no room for a reason.
★ R1742 and then R1747 closed the two live cases rather than the
distinction: `lab` and `packets` both publish now, so no section is
`unspecified` at all. Kept open because
the type is unchanged and the next screen with a specification it
cannot publish yet would be silent in exactly the same way. Worth
noting that the repair is now HALF built: a SURFACE can say why it
is not judged (`Built::Away`) and a SECTION still cannot. Stated
rather than papered over: the honest fix is a declared absence that
carries its reason, the way a closed destination's does — and the
shape to copy is one level down in the same module.

owed.sentence: the report is built on demand and nothing caches or invalidates it
why: Every read walks the roster and asks each mounted screen, which for
the two table-backed sections re-parses nothing but does rebuild
their part rosters. It is a wire read at an agent's cadence rather
than a paint-time cost, so it is not on any frame budget measured so
far — but that is an argument from where it is called, not a
measurement of what it costs, and it is written down as such.
⚠ R1742 made it heavier and says so rather than leaving the sentence
above to age: the third answering section now PARSES its pin on every
read (`include_str!` + a JSON parse) and then scans that surface's
recorded marks once per specified surface. Still a wire read and
still unmeasured — which is the entry, unchanged in kind. The cheap
half is obvious when somebody does measure: the parsed document is a
constant and belongs behind a `OnceCell`.
⚠ R1747 made it heavier again, by the same amount and for the same
reason: a FOURTH section now parses a pin per read, and its own
readings scan the recorded marks more than once per surface. Two
sections doing this was a note; four is a shape, and the shape is
that every section added from here will do it. Still unmeasured, and
the note is now the older of the two facts in this entry.
